why: One coffee raises alertness in a loud place just as at home; the crowd does not cancel it.
source: Smith 2002 Food Chem Toxicol 40:1243; Nehlig 2010 J Alzheimers Dis 20:S85

why: Two drinks blunt the tension of a crowded, noisy setting (stress-response dampening).
source: Sher & Levenson 1982 J Abnorm Psychol 91:350; Sayette 1993 Psychol Bull 114:459

why: 5 mg diazepam takes some of the edge off a stressful crowded place in a non-anxious person.
source: Griffiths & Weerts 1997 Psychopharmacology 134:1; de Wit et al. 1984 Psychopharmacology 83:196

why: When overload drives anxiety high there is more anxiety to relieve, so the same 5 mg gives a bigger drop.
source: Griffiths & Weerts 1997 Psychopharmacology 134:1; Gomez et al. 2018 Expert Opin Pharmacother 19:883 (larger benzodiazepine effects when anxiety is high)

why: Propranolol dampens the racing-heart side of overload, which some autistic adults find calming; evidence is small trials.
source: Beversdorf et al. 2008 J Autism Dev Disord 38:1128 (small trials; anxiety effect inferred)

why: 200 mg theanine gave small reductions in stress feelings in a few small trials; many show nothing.
source: Kimura et al. 2007 Biol Psychol 74:39; Williams et al. 2020 Plant Foods Hum Nutr 75:12 (review)

why: A few puffs (low THC) slightly reduced stress feelings in a lab stressor; low doses are the anxiolytic end of THC's biphasic curve.
source: Childs, Lutz & de Wit 2017 Drug Alcohol Depend 177:136 (7.5 mg THC)

why: A heavy dose of THC in a loud crowded place is a classic recipe for anxiety and paranoia.
source: Childs et al. 2017 Drug Alcohol Depend 177:136 (12.5 mg raised anxiety); D'Souza et al. 2004 Neuropsychopharmacology 29:1558; Freeman et al. 2015 Lancet Psychiatry 2:525

why: 25 mg CBD is far below the ~300 mg doses that reduced anxiety in lab stress tests; lower doses did not work.
source: Zuardi et al. 2017 Front Pharmacol 8:259 (inverted U: 150 and 600 mg ineffective, 300 mg effective); Linares et al. 2019 Braz J Psychiatry 41:9

why: An alpha-2A agonist lowers noradrenaline release and causes mild sedation after a single 1 mg dose.
source: Arnsten et al. 1988 J Neurosci 8:4287; Hunt et al. 1995 J Am Acad Child Adolesc Psychiatry 34:50; guanfacine IR label (somnolence)

why: A loud, bright crowd is a mild stressor for most people.
source: Stansfeld & Matheson 2003 Br Med Bull 68:243 (noise and annoyance/stress)

why: Autistic people report stronger distress in noisy, bright, crowded places; sensory over-responsivity is tied to anxiety.
source: Green & Ben-Sasson 2010 J Autism Dev Disord 40:1495; MacLennan et al. 2020 Autism 24:1066

why: Overload uses up attention, so concentration in a loud crowd drops more for autistic than typical people.
source: Remington et al. 2012 J Abnorm Psychol 121:1009 (mixed); Tavassoli et al. 2014 Autism 18:428; Robertson & Baron-Cohen 2017 Nat Rev Neurosci 18:671

why: Propranolol blocks the pounding heart and shaking of acute stress; reduction in felt anxiety is modest and inconsistent.
source: Steenen et al. 2016 J Psychopharmacol 30:128 (systematic review); Brantigan et al. 1982 Am J Med 72:88

why: In anxious people propranolol mainly helps the bodily symptoms; trials in generalised anxiety show little benefit on worry.
source: Steenen et al. 2016 J Psychopharmacol 30:128; Tyrer & Lader 1974 Br Med J 2:14

why: Benzodiazepines blunt subjective stress responses to lab stressors.
source: Griffiths & Weerts 1997 Psychopharmacology 134:1 (benzodiazepine subjective effects review)

why: With generalised anxiety plus a stressor, a benzodiazepine produces a clear anxiety reduction.
source: Gomez et al. 2018 Expert Opin Pharmacother 19:883 (benzodiazepines in GAD, meta-analysis); Rickels et al. 1983 JAMA 250:767

why: Moderate alcohol dampens the emotional response to a stressor.
source: Sher & Levenson 1982 J Abnorm Psychol 91:350; Sayette 1993 Psychol Bull 114:459; Bradford et al. 2013 Biol Psychiatry 74:e1

why: Caffeine adds to stress arousal (cortisol, blood pressure); felt anxiety rises only a little at one coffee.
source: Lovallo et al. 2006 Psychosom Med 68:734; Childs & de Wit 2006 Psychopharmacology 185:514

why: Having a warm friend present buffers the anxiety of a stressor.
source: Heinrichs et al. 2003 Biol Psychiatry 54:1389; Ditzen et al. 2007 Psychoneuroendocrinology 32:565

why: Two drinks in the evening make people drowsy and fall asleep faster.
source: Ebrahim et al. 2013 Alcohol Clin Exp Res 37:539; Roehrs & Roth 2001 Sleep Med Rev 5:287

why: Hangover brings low mood and malaise the next morning.
source: Penning et al. 2012 Curr Drug Abuse Rev 3:68; van Schrojenstein Lantman et al. 2016 Curr Drug Abuse Rev 9:148

why: "Hangxiety": next-morning anxiety rises after heavy drinking, more so in shy people.
source: Marsh et al. 2019 Pers Individ Dif 147:211

why: Shorter, lighter sleep after late caffeine leaves a little more sleepiness the next morning, though residual caffeine partly masks it.
source: Drake et al. 2013 J Clin Sleep Med 9:1195; Clark & Landolt 2017 Sleep Med Rev 31:70

why: 10 mg diazepam at night has a long half-life and leaves next-day drowsiness (hangover).
source: Vermeeren 2004 CNS Drugs 18:297 (residual effects of hypnotics)

why: Low-dose melatonin is cleared within hours and causes no measurable next-morning hangover.
source: Buscemi et al. 2005 J Gen Intern Med 20:1151; Ferracioli-Oda et al. 2013 PLoS One 8:e63773

why: MDMA keeps people awake and disrupts the night, so they feel tired the next day.
source: Parrott & Lasky 1998 Psychopharmacology 139:261; Huxster et al. 2006 Prog Neuropsychopharmacol Biol Psychiatry 30:469

why: After 4 weeks sertraline lifts mood in depression; much of the average gain is shared with placebo, so the drug-only part is small to medium.
source: Cipriani et al. 2018 Lancet 391:1357; Cipriani et al. 2009 Lancet 373:746

why: SSRIs reduce generalised anxiety after several weeks.
source: Slee et al. 2019 Lancet 393:768 (GAD network meta-analysis); Brawman-Mintzer et al. 2006 J Clin Psychiatry 67:874

why: Bupropion is as effective as SSRIs for depression after weeks of use.
source: Cipriani et al. 2018 Lancet 391:1357; Thase et al. 2005 J Clin Psychiatry 66:974

why: The MAO inhibitor phenelzine (at a therapeutic 30 mg/day) is an effective antidepressant, especially in atypical depression.
source: Thase et al. 1995 Arch Gen Psychiatry 52:1027 (meta-analysis); Liebowitz et al. 1988 Arch Gen Psychiatry 45:129

why: Semaglutide clearly reduces appetite and food intake.
source: Blundell et al. 2017 Diabetes Obes Metab 19:1242; Friedrichsen et al. 2021 Diabetes Obes Metab 23:754

why: Large trials found no change in depression or mood scores on semaglutide.
source: Wadden et al. 2024 JAMA Intern Med 184:1290 (STEP 1-3, 5 pooled psychiatric analysis)

why: Daily coffee drinkers mostly just restore the alertness lost overnight; compared with never-users they are not more alert.
source: James & Rogers 2005 Psychopharmacology 182:1; Rogers et al. 2013 Psychopharmacology 226:229

why: Regular smokers report slightly more anxiety than non-smokers, and anxiety falls after quitting.
source: Taylor et al. 2014 BMJ 348:g1151; Parrott 1999 Am Psychol 54:817

why: Heavy daily drinking raises baseline anxiety through repeated mini-withdrawals and adaptation.
source: Becker 2008 Alcohol Res Health 31:348; Schuckit & Hesselbrock 1994 Am J Psychiatry 151:1723

why: Exercise treatment produces moderate improvements in depression, similar to psychotherapy or drugs.
source: Noetel et al. 2024 BMJ 384:e075847; Schuch et al. 2016 J Psychiatr Res 77:42

why: Daily bright light helps depression, strongly for winter depression and modestly for non-seasonal depression.
source: Golden et al. 2005 Am J Psychiatry 162:656; Tao et al. 2020 J Affect Disord 274:1061

why: Guanfacine helps ADHD attention, but less than stimulants.
source: Hirota et al. 2014 J Am Acad Child Adolesc Psychiatry 53:153; Cortese et al. 2018 Lancet Psychiatry 5:727

why: Methylphenidate keeps improving ADHD attention over weeks with little tolerance at therapeutic doses.
source: Cortese et al. 2018 Lancet Psychiatry 5:727; Storebo et al. 2015 BMJ 351:h5203

why: Reduced appetite is the commonest side effect of daily methylphenidate.
source: Storebo et al. 2015 BMJ 351:h5203; Cortese et al. 2018 Lancet Psychiatry 5:727

why: Stopping regular caffeine causes fatigue and low energy for a few days.
source: Juliano & Griffiths 2004 Psychopharmacology 176:1

why: Drowsiness is one of the most reliable caffeine withdrawal symptoms.
source: Juliano & Griffiths 2004 Psychopharmacology 176:1; James & Rogers 2005 Psychopharmacology 182:1

why: Anxiety, irritability and restlessness peak in the first days after quitting.
source: Hughes 2007 Nicotine Tob Res 9:315; DSM-5 tobacco withdrawal

why: Depressed mood is a core early nicotine withdrawal symptom.
source: Hughes 2007 Nicotine Tob Res 9:315

why: Increased appetite is a classic sign of quitting smoking.
source: Hughes 2007 Nicotine Tob Res 9:315

why: After two weeks of heavy drinking, stopping produces rebound anxiety and tension.
source: Becker 2008 Alcohol Res Health 31:348; Heilig et al. 2010 Addict Biol 15:169

why: Withdrawal does not suppress breathing; if anything respiration rises with sympathetic overdrive.
source: Sullivan et al. 1989 Br J Addict 84:1353; Schuckit 2014 N Engl J Med 371:2109

why: Stopping opioids leaves people more pain-sensitive than before (withdrawal hyperalgesia).
source: Angst & Clark 2006 Anesthesiology 104:570; Compton et al. 2003 Drug Alcohol Depend 70:S29

why: Heroin withdrawal is intensely anxious and restless.
source: Kosten & George 2002 Sci Pract Perspect 1:13; Wesson & Ling 2003 J Psychoactive Drugs 35:253

why: Stopping daily cannabis causes nervousness and irritability for several days.
source: Budney et al. 2004 Am J Psychiatry 161:1967; Bonnet & Preuss 2017 Subst Abuse Rehabil 8:9

why: Reduced appetite is a typical cannabis withdrawal symptom.
source: Budney et al. 2004 Am J Psychiatry 161:1967; Haney et al. 1999 Psychopharmacology 141:395

why: After stopping regular amphetamine people sleep more and feel drowsy; this is mild after modest doses.
source: McGregor et al. 2005 Addiction 100:1320; Shoptaw et al. 2009 Cochrane CD003021

why: A single dose of methylphenidate clearly improves attention in ADHD.
source: Cortese et al. 2018 Lancet Psychiatry 5:727; Storebo et al. 2015 BMJ 351:h5203

why: In ADHD, methylphenidate does not on average increase anxiety; a meta-analysis found anxiety slightly lower on stimulants.
source: Coughlin et al. 2015 J Child Adolesc Psychopharmacol 25:611

why: Caffeine counters sleepiness more when people are short of sleep, because there is more sleepiness to counter.
source: Bonnet et al. 2005 Sleep 28:1144; McLellan et al. 2016 Neurosci Biobehav Rev 71:294

why: One ketamine infusion produces a rapid antidepressant effect that is clear at 24 hours.
source: Berman et al. 2000 Biol Psychiatry 47:351; Zarate et al. 2006 Arch Gen Psychiatry 63:856; McGirr et al. 2015 Psychol Med 45:693

why: In healthy volunteers, mood is back to normal a day after a ketamine infusion.
source: Krystal et al. 1994 Arch Gen Psychiatry 51:199 (effects resolve within hours in healthy volunteers)

why: A single psilocybin session with support lifts mood in depression for at least a week.
source: Goodwin et al. 2022 N Engl J Med 387:1637; Davis et al. 2021 JAMA Psychiatry 78:481

why: Blocking dopamine D2 receptors reduces drive and willingness to work for rewards.
source: Pessiglione et al. 2006 Nature 442:1042; Artaloytia et al. 2006 Biol Psychiatry 59:115
